_comment: Complaints from tools/analyze.py's gate that build.check_quality prints but
does not stop the build for. Everything here is a real defect - the point is
that it is a defect somebody has already looked at and decided to carry, not
Only complaints the ratchet cannot express belong here. A number that got
worse is caught by metrics-baseline.json and must not be silenced by adding a
line to this file; these are the ones that carry no number, so they are raised
unconditionally on every run and would otherwise wedge the build shut for good.
Matching ignores runs of whitespace, so the alignment analyze.py pads with does
not have to be reproduced exactly. Delete a line the day the defect is fixed -
a stale entry here is a hole in the gate.
Empty since the gate grew a class for it: a fold the tracker cannot resolve
is reported as `unmeasured`, on its own, because it is a state of the
instrument and not a defect of the render. The notes below are kept - they
still say what fixing each one would mean.

notes.AppStarting unmeasured, closed 2026-08-2: Both AppStarting entries - jitter_unmeasured and fold_unmeasured - are gone, and neither was closed by a change to the render. They were the dark-line tracker's state. That instrument takes the darkest interior pixel of a row with a prominence around it, which is a feature the author never drew: his own frames read unmeasured by it at every size on every wedge. AppStarting's crease is the faintest in the set, so it was the first to stop resolving. The step-aware fit that replaced it as the acceptance reading (tools/foldfit.py) reads 20 stations of 24 at 128, 256 and 512, and all 27 frames of the cycle at full pair coverage, so the fold and the jitter are both measured now. What the numbers say is a separate question and is carried as debt: unres 0.60, s_conv 3.67. The old notes said fixing this meant a tracker that can read both sides rather than putting the tail hook back - that is what happened.
notes.baseline provenance 2026-08-22: Reshot again, and this file now means: the accepted renderer measured by the product-frame fold contract. Two independent events forced it, and both are named on purpose. First the measurement changed (b30f091, 816fd02): the fold contract used to read hybrid.frame_image at the nine authored indices, which for Hand, Wait and AppStarting is nine pictures that ship nowhere - the loop is lit from one canonical render, and the frames that reach the user are 27 reconstructions of it. Everything temporal and everything about the fold now goes through analyze.product_cycle, and the author is read at each frame's own phase rather than at index // 3. Second the renderer changed (08a4907): _fold_restep replaces the wedges' fold transition, which was 0.02..0.05 logical units - the pixel pitch, not a width - with the author's own 0.60. The audit before the reshot: 106 numbers moved of 972 that both files carry, 312 keys left and 3423 arrived. The departures are the dark-line tracker losing the line it was built to follow, on a render that deliberately no longer draws one (Arrow, Hand, UpArrow and Wait now read legacy jag, gap, wander and luma_step as zero because nothing resolves; Arrow_Down's rows fall 122 to 8; AppStarting's legacy tracker starts resolving where it did not, at jag 108.4, which is worth watching and gates nothing). The arrivals are the step-aware readings on 27 product frames. Of the rest, delta_e moves by at most 3 percent on the cursors whose cross-section changed, which is the change. Nothing moved that could not be named. The gate against the new file: nothing changed, bad 0, debt 16, unmeasured empty.
notes.baseline provenance: metrics-baseline.json was reshot 2026-08-21 against renderer commit bd3197b, replacing a snapshot taken at dd46b61. Nearly every number in the file moved, and that is expected rather than alarming: six render-affecting commits had landed in between - the Handwriting material layer, its luma-only restriction, the NO saturation change, the thin-element glass lift, the static wedge tip level, and the material DC fix. The large movements were audited before the reshot was accepted and none was an unexplained regression: density went 0.109 to 0.205 percent against a 2.0 threshold, tip at 64px fell 3.2 to 0 on four wedges (that number is the gap between the point and where the fold reaches it, so zero is the fold arriving), delta_e improved on NO, IBeam, SizeAll and SizeNESW, and AppStarting's inner_jitter rows went to zero, which is the tracker state already carried as unmeasured. Reshoot the file whenever it drifts this far again - a baseline several accepted commits behind stops being a snapshot of the product and becomes a mixture of eras, and the gate then guards a renderer nobody ships.
notes.Handwriting delta_e baseline: Not a defect - a warning about the number itself. The pre-2026-08-21 baseline had Handwriting at 3.553, and that value does not carry forward as a quality target: frames 3-5 were in hybrid._BROKEN_COLOUR then and drew their colour from the author's own 32px frame upscaled, while delta_e is measured against that same frame downsampled back, so it was largely comparing the author with himself through a resampler. The baseline was retaken at 3.895 after the material layer's DC invariant was restored (NEXT.md 47, 48). A future run that reads 3.5 on these frames has probably lost the render, not improved it.
notes.baseline provenance 2026-08-22, NO ring: Reshot again, and this file now means: the prohibition sign redrawn from the author's template (7acb142), measured by a cadence gate that compares against him step by step (187e642). Two events again, and both are named on purpose. The instrument first: morph_peak is peak over mean, and it is not monotone in quality - _no_ring left NO's largest frame-to-frame step at 52.09, exactly where main had it, and every step it did touch moved toward the author (42.37 to 38.47 against his 17.04, 32.59 to 13.42 against 16.03, 17.55 to 4.64 against 6.40), yet the ratio read worse because the mean fell with them. It is diagnostic now; morph_cadence_err and morph_peak_abs decide, both as pure ratchets with no absolute target, because the remaster's steps run 2-3x his on every morph and any constant written today would be written to fit that. Then the renderer: _no_ring replaces the sign's coverage and colour together - see DEAD_ENDS.md for why neither half may ship alone. The audit before the reshot: 3 numbers moved of 372 that both files carry, none left, 4 arrived. All three departures are NO and all three are the change - delta_e 5.972 to 5.541, cadence 1.974 to 2.315 (the ratio, now diagnostic), and ghost_rgb 0.026 to 0.035, which is the stage writing the stroke's colour across the whole disc including pixels the alpha leaves empty; it is a thirtieth of its threshold and is ratcheted from here. The four arrivals are the two new readings on the two cursors that morph. Nothing else in the set moved by a thousandth.
notes.baseline provenance 2026-08-22, morph st: Reshot a second time the same day, and only four numbers moved: morph_cadence_err and morph_peak_abs on the two cursors that morph. Nothing else in the 376 the two files share changed by a thousandth, nothing left and nothing arrived, and cadence and ghost_rgb in particular did not move - they still come off the old _deltas, and their standing still is the check that the migration did not reach into a pipeline that was not its business. What changed is how a morph's steps are measured. _deltas averages over pixels above a fraction of the pair's own peak alpha, and the author's peak is 249..255 where ours is 222..248, so his sample and ours were different pixels in different numbers - on NO's third step his held one pixel and ours thirty-six, and a mean over one pixel is not a cadence. _morph_visible_steps composites every frame onto white, grey and black on the 32x32 grid the author drew at and averages the absolute difference over all pixels, channels and backgrounds: no mask, no threshold, and the same denominator for him, for us and for every step. NO's apparent 5->6 outlier was an artefact of the old sample and is gone - 7.615 for him against 7.633 for us, with both cycles peaking at 8->9. The values recorded here are therefore not comparable with the ones in the note above; they are a different instrument, not a different render.
notes.baseline provenance 2026-08-22, sign pai: Third reshot of the day, three numbers moved, all NO and all improvements: cadence 2.3154 to 2.2391, ghost_rgb 0.0355 to 0.0323, morph_cadence_err 0.1966 to 0.1928. Nothing else of the 376 moved, nothing left, nothing arrived. The change is that _no_ring stopped painting glass. It writes the sign's one red across the whole disc on purpose - the bar and the ring are the same colour on his art, measured at 0.23, 0.27, 0.08 and 0.01 of delta_e apart on the four frames, and recolouring only the ring would seam where they cross - but most of what shows inside the hole is the pointer, and painting that cost up to 0.7 of delta_e there against main. The paint is now scaled by whether the sign has material at that pixel: the analytic ring's coverage, or the pixel's own colourfulness on the same calibration the pointer mask uses. No new constant. Every zone improved on every frame - NO[7] 4.626 to 4.377, [9] 3.821 to 3.562, [10] 3.478 to 3.240, and the pointer inside the hole 10.140 to 9.451. delta_e in this file does not move, because the number it records for NO is frame 5's 5.541 and the sign has no ring there yet.
